sections.title: Common EV and Hybrid Safety Questions

items.title: What is a PHEV?
body: A Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV) uses both an electric motor and a gas engine, and you can recharge the battery by plugging it in.

items.title: What is an HEV?
body: A Hybrid Electric Vehicle (HEV) also combines electric and gas power, but it recharges through driving, no plug-in required.

items.title: What is a BEV?
body: A Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV) runs fully on electricity and uses a high-voltage battery as its only power source.

items.title: What is an EREV?
body: An Extended-Range Electric Vehicle (EREV) drives mainly on electric power but includes a small gas engine that generates electricity when needed.

items.title: How do I become an EV technician?
body: Becoming an EV technician requires OEM-specific training and certifications based on the vehicles you plan to service. Many technicians also complete post-secondary automotive or EV training programs.

items.title: How is EV collision repair different from repairing hybrid or gas vehicles?
body: EV collision repair involves unique intake steps, safety requirements, and repair procedures. Technicians must complete proper training and follow OEM-specified service information.

items.title: How is hybrid collision repair different from repairing EVs or gas vehicles?
body: Hybrid collision repair involves unique intake steps, safety requirements, and repair procedures. Technicians must complete proper training and follow OEM-specified service information.

items.title: Can any body shop fix a hybrid or electric vehicle?
body: Yes, as long as the shop has the required OEM training and follows all OEM-outlined repair procedures.

items.title: What certifications should a shop have to safely repair hybrid or electric vehicles?
body: Certification requirements vary by OEM. I‑CAR offers hybrid and EV-specific training and certifications developed with individual manufacturers.

items.title: What are the most common issues in EV repair?
body: Most issues occur when proper procedures or required safety steps are not followed.

items.title: What are the main risks involved in hybrid or electric vehicle repairs?
body: Hybrid and electric vehicles contain high voltage components and architecture that have special repair and maintenance considerations. Only trained, certified technicians and shops should perform these repairs.

items.title: What safety precautions are needed after a hybrid or electric vehicle collision?
body: Shops must follow OEM-specified post-collision requirements, which may include high-voltage disablement, battery assessments, and other safety steps.
